set.per_unit_cap: Revenue and Taxation Code 214(g)(1)(C) caps the exemption at $20,000,000 of assessed value per taxpayer per fiscal year (single or multiple properties), and only where the exemption rests solely on the 90 percent lower income occupancy test for a property not owned by a limited partnership. Projects with tax-exempt bonds, government loans or grants (214(g)(1)(A)) or low-income housing tax credits (214(g)(1)(B)) are outside the cap; LP-owned projects with a nonprofit managing general partner must have tax credits or government financing to qualify (BOE Publication 149). Not a statewide cap.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: 24 CFR 983.153(c) (HUD PBV development requirements, labor standards): for development activity (new construction or rehabilitation) involving nine or more PBV contract units, the owner and its contractors must pay Davis-Bacon wages and the PHA monitors compliance; existing-housing PBV contracts with no development activity do not trigger it. SHRA's draft 2027 HCV Administrative Plan (Chapter 21) states the PHA will project-base units in new construction, rehabilitation and existing projects as defined in an RFP, so PBV awards to new construction or rehab of 9+ contract units carry Davis-Bacon. https://www.shra.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/SHRA-HCV-2027-Admin-Plan-Draft.pdf https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/983.153

reason: SHRA Admin Plan Chapter 21 allows PBVs in new construction and rehab, so 24 CFR 983.153(c) Davis-Bacon applies at 9+ contract units.
